newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit hits four-month high on speculative buying. [CORRECTED 7:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Ringgit hits four-month high on speculative buying. [CORRECTED 7:55 GMT]

text.p: The Malaysian ringgit hit a four-month high against the U.S. dollar in New York overnight, powered by widespread speculative buying in the first rally of the new year, foreign exchange dealers said on Tuesday.

Rumours of Malaysia's central bank, Bank Negara, intervening during New York trading hours halted the rise and triggered profit-taking. The ringgit touched a high of 2.4940/50 per dollar against 2.5218 at close of trading on Friday.
By noon on Tuesday, the Malaysian unit retreated to 2.4995/05 to the dollar on profit-taking.
No confirmation of intervention could be obtained from Bank Negara.
"Everybody seems to have jumped on to the dollar/ringgit bandwagon," said a dealer with a Singapore-based European bank.
He said what started as ringgit/Singapore dollar operation early on Monday had turned into a bull run for the ringgit.
"Singaporeans who had gone long (on the Singapore dollar) to keep the unit stable before the Singapore elections (on January 2) are returning to ringgit," a dealer with a Malaysian bank said.
With a renewed perception of stability in Singapore after the ruling People's Action Party was returned to power last week, normal trading activity has resumed, he said.
"They are going back to ringgit in particular for its high yield and strong economic fundamentals," the dealer said.
The benchmark three-month interbank rate in Kuala Lumpur is more than four percentage points higher than in Singapore.
The ringgit has gained over 250 points to around 1.7790/7810 per Singapore dollar in the last two days.
By Monday afternoon, many in London started buying the ringgit against the U.S. dollar, mainly for speculative play. This started a widespread move into the ringgit.
Dealers said while the market had expected a good year for the ringgit, the bull run had come much earlier than anticipated, which would limit further rises of the currency and induce consolidation.
"It is losing momentum for the time being. Not many will buy ringgit at this level," said the head of foreign exchange dealing at a Malaysian bank.
"The profit-taking is mainly out of Kuala Lumpur," he said.
"Dollar/ringgit should consolidate around the present levels unless the dollar comes off against other major currencies," another dealer said.
"After a massive overnight fall, U.S. dollar/ringgit seems consolidative within 2.4980 (corrects) and 2.5020 range for the short-term," research firm I.D.E.A. said in a technical report.
It said the rise was in line with its survey of several banks last week, which suggested that the ringgit would be the favourite currency of the region this year.
The two main factors that investors find attractive in the ringgit were an improvement in the country's trade balance and a cooling down of its racing economy.

Malaysia's 1996 gross domestic product growth is expected to fall to 8.2 percent, following 9.5 percent growth in 1995. The country has reported nine straight years of growth over eight percent, which is expected to be maintained until the year 2000.
Malaysia recorded a sharply lower trade deficit of 954.35 million ringgit ($378.7 million) in the first 10 months of 1996 against around 9.96 billion in the corresponding period of 1995.
The country's growing current account deficit and inflation had triggered worries about overheating last year and forced it to maintain a high interest rate regime and to slow growth.
-- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-230 7509)
